LESSON: WATER

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Resources in Our Environment
Topic 3.1: Water
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Water, part of Resources in Our Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can we use water without wasting it? 2. Why do we care for water sources?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Water together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner models water sources in class learning space or corner using locally available materials.

Creativity and imagination: learner develops originality skills as they model, draw and colour different sources of water.

Values:
Unity: A learner enhances equality as they display team spirit when they participate in school water day to share experiences on using water

sparingly.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Health promotion issues: learner drinks clean water and role play using water sparingly for personal wellbeing.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Making a poster on water conservation at home and school draws knowledge from writing skills in Language Activities.

Suggested Learning Resources

Approved learning support materials, digital devices with assistive technology, manilla papers, crayons, pencils, clay soil, modelling clay,

water, local environment, water sources, containers.
